date_note: ComputerBase (published 2026-11-26) says the US Justice Department announced on Wednesday; read as 25 November.
title: ComputerBase: US charges RansomwareHelp co-founder over alleged ransom payments to attackers
geo_basis: state: ComputerBase calls the firm Florida-based
summary: ComputerBase reports, citing the US Justice Department, that RansomwareHelp co-founder and CTO Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar faces charges over allegedly paying attackers in Bitcoin for victims while the firm promised data recovery without ransom. The firm's website said 'Do not pay the ransom!'. ComputerBase notes the presumption of innocence applies.
plain: ComputerBase reports that the US charged the co-founder of a data-recovery firm that promised not to pay ransom. He allegedly paid the attackers anyway. The presumption of innocence applies.
exec: Firms hiring data-recovery help after ransomware may be paying attackers without knowing, according to the US allegations as ComputerBase reports them.

sources.name: ComputerBase: RansomwareHelp: Datenretter sollen heimlich Lösegeld an Hacker gezahlt haben

validation.note: One publisher read (ComputerBase, relaying the DOJ announcement and Krebs). The DOJ page itself was not read.
